findings.title: Mandatory canonical-record and mirror assertions are introduced before lifecycle/domain completeness is established
findings.evidence: Every mobile&&!of_city query now requires a named canonical record. Empty IDs, no Movers, issued-without-record, retired/unknown IDs and incomplete records become refusals; the document explicitly calls this a new refusal on unreached/no-group/pre-bind/wreck states. The legitimate unhosted movement branch is still retained, while canonical registration is supplied through the group roster/link lifecycle. The closed observer reached only alive, recorded kind1 offers and cannot establish availability or synchronization for every supported caller/creation/placement/lifetime path. The new mirror assertion additionally turns any legitimate producer not yet incorporated into the canonical lifecycle into an engine fatal.
findings.impact: Previously decidable collisions can be stopped by a newly required registry/identity state, or by a valid Core writer whose canonical update has not been covered. NoID/unrecorded/dead/unreached cannot be reclassified as invalid merely because the one observed default window had none. Genuinely invalid stale/forged IDs may still be refused; they must be distinguished from legitimate supported paths by source/lifecycle evidence.
findings.minimum_correction: Establish canonical availability and coherent physical pose/vector updates for legitimate paths before their first collision question, at actual creation/binding/placement/step/skipped-update/lifetime boundaries. Preserve formerly valid default/unhosted/pre-bind/wreck behavior or provide decisive current compiled caller/lifecycle proof that a particular category is genuinely invalid there. Do not query-seed from Core words, invent zeros/derived vectors, weaken the old physical oracle, or treat a new expected-refusal test and a kind1-only sample as the compatibility proof. Keep every unreached writer/domain explicitly required.
findings.validation_boundary: Use coherent positive consumption/default and relevant lifecycle controls before damaged/refusal cases. The current C control still accepts a no-ID offer under a scripted candidate host, while the new real-provider test declares it refused; those controls do not demonstrate preserved end-to-end compatibility.

findings.title: New canonical dispatch evaluates raw floating flag words before their finite/domain validation
findings.evidence: transport_pose intentionally accepts arbitrary word patterns. The new flag closure performs f32::from_bits(words[MOBILE/OF_CITY/PLACEMENT_GIVEN]) !=0.0 before the existing candidate validator. A signaling NaN therefore has no explicit safe raw-classification barrier before a possible FP comparison, and finite malformed nonzero flags can select canonical lookup/refusal before their request-domain error. The model callback itself has no per-callback floating-state guard.
findings.impact: Malformed input can affect floating status/trap behavior or produce a registry/busy/missing-record result before the actual malformed-request diagnosis. This is a source-level ordering/boundary defect; no bad native execution or claimed observed trap was used to establish it, and a compiler optimization is not a raw-word safety guarantee.
findings.minimum_correction: Classify the relevant raw finite and flag domains before any floating evaluation or canonical lookup, reusing the established request classifier/raw-word discipline and preserving the prior accepted zero/flag semantics. Only then select the registry path. Validate the decision controls without accidentally reintroducing discarded mirror words as physical authority.
findings.validation_boundary: One positive-first malformed signaling-NaN/invalid flag case at the existing real-provider boundary, with the intended request error winning before record lookup, is enough for this finding. No unsafe old-native or new broad FP programme is required.

new_dataflow_assessment: The intended canonical consumption is real in the inspected code: the provider reads the same SharedMovers handle used by movement and overwrites the mobile candidate decision inputs with record position/motion and stage-permitted attitude. It does not add a ModelStore pose cache. The real-provider unit deliberately supplies different mirror words and observes the canonical decision/pose, then moves the same record and observes the next decision change. This is meaningful consumption evidence at that unit boundary.

Routed end-of-step and the two existing vector-derivation early returns now obtain motion from a Host step/result, rather than copying a Core-derived vector into the query. The new Host calculation is the original row2-times-speed expression over its own post-step record. Bind seeds and explicit placement inputs are now carried for every recognized hosted kind; ship results and lifecycle-held vectors are retained. Signed zeros and stale-vector-until-derivation behavior have focused tests.

The existing first lifecycle claim still adopts the Core-origin vector; the source itself declares that remaining producer responsibility. Explicit placements remain inputs from the campaign. Neither this partial retention change nor the canonical query makes all physical producers, backing state or writers Host-owned.

The original physical getter staging and scan/first-hit implementation are not otherwise changed. UPDATED whole-flag effects and the shared terrain record remain in their existing requested positions. Host ID lookup is now once per offer; the same bounded ID travels in each question and is echoed in the real C collaborator. No prior caller output words are read.

Borrowed IDs are copied into synchronous bounded request storage. Reference-model canonical lookup uses try_borrow and copies words before the borrow ends; no new pointer/index wire or second registry was found. The public witness mutates the Host registry before delegating the relevant reference question, rather than while its read borrow is active.

No additional concrete memory/RefCell/store/layout bug was established. The new physical multiplications execute in the existing Host movement arithmetic context; the focused same-expression tests are not a new full public caller-FP/parity measurement. The unchecked flag ordering above remains the concrete new FP boundary issue.
